root_cause.text: A lock ordering violation in ntfs3 compressed read path caused ntfs_read_folio() to take the inode mutex ni_lock before ni_read_folio_cmpr() locked all pages in the compressed frame, enabling an ni_lock ↔ page-lock inversion deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly describes Task A holding ni_lock then waiting on page Y while Task B holds page Y and waits on ni_lock, and the patch moves ni_lock acquisition out of ntfs_read_folio() and into ni_read_folio_cmpr() only after the frame’s page locks are acquired (`ni_lock(ni); err = ni_read_frame(...); ni_unlock(ni);`).

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: A lock ordering violation in ntfs3 compressed read path caused ntfs_read_folio() to take the inode mutex ni_lock before ni_read_folio_cmpr() locked all pages in the compressed frame, enabling an ni_lock ↔ page-lock inversion deadlock.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly describes Task A holding ni_lock then waiting on page Y while Task B holds page Y and waits on ni_lock, and the patch moves ni_lock acquisition out of ntfs_read_folio() and into ni_read_folio_cmpr() only after the frame’s page locks are acquired (`ni_lock(ni); err = ni_read_frame(...); ni_unlock(ni);`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect ni_read_frame() with the inode lock in ni_read_folio_cmpr() to prevent races during compressed frame reads.
intent_record.what: A lock and unlock pair was added around the call to ni_read_frame() in ni_read_folio_cmpr(), specifically inserting ni_lock(ni) before the call and ni_unlock(ni) after it.
intent_record.how: This change serializes access to the ntfs_inode while reading a compressed frame, preventing concurrent operations on the same inode from racing with ni_read_frame() and causing inconsistent state or unsafe execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compressed folio reads by removing external ni locking and letting ni_read_folio_cmpr acquire the lock in the proper order.
intent_record.what: In the compressed-file branch of ntfs_read_folio(), the explicit ni_lock(ni) and ni_unlock(ni) calls around ni_read_folio_cmpr(ni, folio) were removed, and a comment was added stating that ni_lock is taken inside ni_read_folio_cmpr after page locks.
intent_record.how: This changes locking so the inode lock is no longer acquired by ntfs_read_folio() before calling the compressed folio read helper, relying instead on ni_read_folio_cmpr() to take the lock at the correct point after page locks are held. At runtime this avoids taking the lock in the wrong order and helps prevent locking/order-related failures such as deadlocks.

grouping_result.intent: Fix compressed folio reads by removing external ni locking and letting ni_read_folio_cmpr acquire the lock in the proper order.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix compressed folio read locking by ensuring ni_read_folio_cmpr() acquires the inode lock internally in the correct order to protect compressed frame reads.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the deadlock root cause by moving inode lock acquisition into ni_read_folio_cmpr() so compressed frame pages can be locked first and ni_lock taken in the correct order, eliminating the ni_lock-to-page-lock inversion in compressed reads.

candidates.rationale: This takes the inode lock in ntfs_read_folio() before entering the compressed read helper, creating the wrong lock order relative to the page locks later taken for the compressed frame and directly enabling the ni_lock ↔ page-lock inversion.

This call is made while ni_lock is already held by the caller, causing ni_read_folio_cmpr() to run under externally imposed inode locking instead of acquiring the lock internally after page locking, which is the core ordering bug.

The compressed frame read occurs here without the helper itself taking ni_lock internally first; combined with callers that already hold ni_lock, this reflects the unsafe locking design that allowed deadlock during frame/page handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires the inode mutex in ntfs_read_folio() before entering the compressed read path. The root cause is the resulting wrong lock order: ni_lock is held first, and then ni_read_folio_cmpr() locks pages in the compressed frame, creating an ni_lock ↔ page-lock inversion deadlock.

This call invokes the compressed folio read helper while ni_lock is already held by the caller. That external locking forces ni_read_folio_cmpr() to execute under the wrong lock ordering instead of acquiring locks in the safe order internally, directly contributing to the deadlock condition.
